title: Private Control Plane Operator Quickstart & Rotation Diary
content:
Purpose

This doc is a practical operator-focused quickstart and day-by-day diary for bootstrapping a Private Control Plane (VPC or on-prem) cluster, scaling it from seed -> production, and procedures for node/KMS/TF rotations and rolling upgrades. It collects the tribal knowledge that helps minimize downtime and preserves KV/prefix cache integrity for serving workloads.

Scope
- Initial infra provisioning using our Terraform modules (edge + controlplane modules)
- Network and KMS setup and validation
- First-time control-plane bootstrap and secrets handoff
- Safe scaling pattern for add/remove operator nodes and GPU pools
- Rotation procedures: operator nodes, service accounts, KMS keys, TLS certs, and Terraform state migration
- Upgrade patterns (canary -> rolling -> rollback) and runbook-driven checks

Audience
- Platform engineers responsible for Private CP installs
- Solutions engineers during customer onboarding
- On-call SREs handling CP incidents

Quick prerequisites checklist (seed deploy)
- Enterprise account + network CIDR plan documented (subnets for controlplane, pods, services)
- Customer-provided KMS/HSM credentials and access window for rotation
- Terraform state backend configured (S3/GCS with locking) and access keys staged
- Inventory of hosts (IP list) and SSH keys for bare-metal installs
- NTP, DNS records, and firewall rules validated
- Slack/SRE pager rotation notified 48h before planned change windows

Terraform module notes (practical flags and pitfalls)
- Module references: use tag pinning to specific module commit (avoid floating branch). Example var: controlplane_module_ref = "git::https://...//modules/controlplane?ref=v1.3.2"
- Backend: enable state locking: terraform { backend "s3" { lock_table = var.tf_lock_table } }
- Sensitive outputs: never output KMS plaintext. Use output with sensitive = true and consume via CI secrets only.
- var:operator_count vs var:operator_autoscale_min: the operator pool must have min=1 and preferred 2 for HA. When you set autoscale, ensure you also set maintenance_windows to avoid simultaneous scale-down during rotation.
- known issue: module version v1.2.x had a race in the node-labeling hook leading to ephemeral reconciliation failures. Workaround: set bootstrap_pause_sec=30 on small clusters. Track upgrade PR that fixed it: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-controlplane-terraform/pull/87

Network & Routing checks
- Confirm /etc/resolv.conf on hosts points to private DNS resolvers.
- Validate inter-subnet MTU and path MTU discovery (we see fragmentation causing websocket disconnects for streaming).
- Security Group rules: allow controlplane -> worker 6443, 10250, and 22 during bootstrap window; later tighten to private VPC ranges.
- Check that floating load-balancer health checks are using the correct interface (host vs mgmt network).

KMS and secrets plan
- Prefer customer-managed KMS keys with rotation window agreed. Document KMS key ARNs in vault reference.
- Staged rotation: create new key/version, rewrap symmetric keys offline, update control plane secret reference, and trigger rolling restart of operator pods.
- NEVER rotate KMS and Terraform state backend at the same time. Sequence: (1) tf state validated -> (2) create new KMS key -> (3) rewrap secrets -> (4) update cluster -> (5) monitor.

Bootstrap sequence (high-level)
1) Preflight checklist (network, tf backend, keys)
2) terraform apply -var-file=customer-vars.tfvars -target=module.network (provision VPC/subnets)
3) terraform apply -target=module.controlplane.bootstrap (provision controlplane hosts + LB)
4) Run bootstrap script on primary operator host: ./bootstrap-controlplane.sh --config /tmp/cp-config.yaml
5) Validate API server reachability: curl -k https://<controlplane-lb>:6443/healthz
6) Apply RBAC + service-accounts using the operator manifests (kubectl apply -f operator-manifests/)
7) Hand off secrets to vault/KMS and confirm encryption for etcd backups
8) Provision initial model-serving GPU pool (dedicated namespace) and a tiny canary traffic route

Scaling from seed to production (safe pattern)
- Pattern: add two new operator nodes at a time, validate, then remove old ones. Do not change more than 25% of operator pool in a single window.
- Steps: terraform apply to add nodes -> wait for nodeReady & operator pods scheduled -> verify controlplane resource usage stable -> promote LB weights to include new nodes -> drain old nodes (kubectl drain --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets <node>) -> terraform destroy old nodes.
- Validate: p50/p95 token latency, error-rate < 0.5%, KV cache hit ratio unchanged +/- 2%, GPU util within expected band.

Operator node rotation checklist (detailed)
- Window: low traffic house window (agree with customer)
- Pre-rotate: snapshot etcd backup + verify restore procedure (test restore in staging monthly)
- Lock autoscaler (set min=max to temporarily freeze scaling)
- For each node in rotation order (see inventory tag rotate-priority):
  a) Mark node unschedulable
  b) Graceful drain (kubectl drain) and wait for in-flight requests to finish (check operator-specific metrics: inflight_requests).
  c) Stop service processes and run disk scrub (if on bare-metal)
  d) Reimage/provision via terraform replace or use image update pipeline
  e) Rejoin cluster and verify operator pod logs for clean start and KV cache warming
  f) Run smoke test: authenticate, simple generation, embedding latency, streaming handshake
- Post-rotate: unlock autoscaler, watch metrics for 1-2 hours

KMS key rotation step-by-step (recommended pretested)
1) Create new key in KMS with correct IAM principals
2) Export key metadata to vault staging path
3) Use controlplane rewrap script to re-encrypt stored symmetric keys: ./rekey.sh --from <old-key> --to <new-key> --dry-run
4) After dry-run verified, rewrap and push new references to secret store
5) Trigger operator rolling-restart via annotation: kubectl -n controlplane rollout restart deployment/operator
6) Verify node logs show KMS key acceptance and no decryption failures
7) Confirm backups encrypted with new key and validate restore (in staging)

Terraform state migration notes
- When migrating backend (e.g., GCS -> S3), use terraform state pull to get the canonical state, verify checksums, then terraform init -backend-config pointing to new backend. Keep both backend access for 24 hours to reconcile any drift.
- Lock the pipeline (pause CI) so no concurrent applies during migration.
- Keep a tfstate snapshot in secure vault and record checksum in ticket (JIRA-PRIVCP-452).

Upgrade plan (controlplane/operator binary and TF modules)
- Non-disruptive sequence: module updates -> infra changes (if needed) -> operator binary update -> canary deployments -> rolling to remainder.
- Canary approach: pick a non-critical routing group (10% of traffic) and upgrade operator pods only on a subset of operator hosts. Wait 30-60m based on traffic; measure errors and latency regressions.
- Metrics gating: p99 latency increase < 10% and error-rate delta < 0.25 percentage points. If breach, rollback immediately to previous pod image via kubectl set image or kubectl rollout undo.
- If TF module changes require node replacement (e.g., kernel flags), prefer blue/green style: provision new node pool, migrate traffic, then decommission old pool.

Rollback play (fast stop)
- If errors escalate after a change: 1) Use LB to route away from new pool 2) Roll pods back (kubectl rollout undo) 3) Restore etcd snapshot if controlplane majority lost 4) Revert Terraform changes via target destroy or apply previous state file
- Keep a tested recovery script at scripts/recovery/fast_restore.sh referenced in README.

Observability and SLO checks (what to watch)
- API server health: /healthz, etcd leader election frequency, etcd commit duration
- Latency: token generation p50/p95/p99 per-route
- Throughput: tokens/sec, open streams
- Errors: 5xxs on generation, websocket disconnects, kv cache misses
- Infra: GPU memory pressure, node OOMs, disk I/O spikes during reimage
- Alerts: create temporary elevated alerts for an upgrade window (reduce noise thresholds to catch regressions)

Troubleshooting notes (frequent quirks)
- Symptom: sudden drop in streaming success after rotation -> likely MTU/path or LB health probe misconfiguration. Check TCP MSS and health check endpoint binding.
- Symptom: operator pods crash-looping with decryption errors -> mismatch KMS key ARN in secret store. Check vault and rewrap logs.
- Symptom: slow token p95 after scaling -> check KV cache cold-start; warm caches by replaying small set of canary requests against new nodes (script: tools/warm_kv_cache.py)

Postmortem diary entries (operator tips)
- 2025-01-21: Seed rollout to customer-xyz failed due to TF module v1.2 race; fixed by bootstrapping with bootstrap_pause_sec=30 and upgraded module to v1.3.0.
- 2025-02-05: KMS rewrap dry-run caught vault ACL missing kms:Decrypt for service-account-cp; ACL fixed on IAM side.

Open questions / TODOs
- Automate KMS rewrap with a safe dry-run + gated merge pipeline (owner: @Ethan)
- Add a warm-cache pre-writes step to Terraform apply pipeline to avoid cold-start latency on scale-ups
- Build a synthetic canary runner that exercises long-running streaming sessions in addition to single-turn generation

Appendix - Helpful commands
- Check controlplane API: curl -k https://<lb>:6443/healthz
- Tail operator logs: kubectl -n controlplane logs -l app=operator -f
- Drain node: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
- Re-provision host using tf replace: terraform apply -replace=module.controlplane.aws_instance.operator[0]
- Rewrap dry-run: ./scripts/rekey.sh --from old-key --to new-key --dry-run

Contact and escalation path
- Primary: Aisha Patel (on-call rotation)
- Secondary: Ravi Kumar
- Pager: #infra-oncall (Slack) -> follow page escalation documented in Confluence

Notes to self (scratchpad)
- Keep this doc short and operator-centric; move long design rationale to confluence link above.
- Sync with solutions-eng before first customer carve-out to ensure network naming conventions match their firewall rules.

End of runbook.
